clue.text: Try hard to keep parking space for boffin

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to exert yourself is to try hard
P is the road-sign symbol marking a parking space

explanation.surface: A determined effort to save a parking spot for a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: A boffin is an informal British term for a clever specialist or scientist, someone highly skilled.

clue.text: Penny's restrained from liking charm

indicators.note: kept back from the word, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a penchant is a liking or fondness
P is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A frugal person resists a liking for a lucky trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to delight or bewitch them, as a spell does.

clue.text: Copper's crafty to dry up

parts.note: a copper is a penny coin, abbreviated P
arch means sly or knowingly cunning

explanation.surface: A cunning police officer is trying to dry out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman or the metal, but here it is a penny coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To parch something is to scorch it until it is thoroughly dehydrated.

clue.text: Comfortable about bridge opponents becoming bitter

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: restful means relaxed and comfortable
in contract bridge East and North are opposing players, E and N

explanation.surface: A relaxed card player turns sour about the opposing pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling resentment means harbouring a grudge, an aggrieved and sour feeling.

clue.text: Fly in son's mobile home

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
a camper is a motor vehicle you can live in

explanation.surface: An insect has got into the boy's camper van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the insect, but it is the verb: to dash off quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly can mean to rush away hurriedly, just as to scamper is to run off quickly.

clue.text: Team leader wears bowler in ship

indicators.note: the bowler wears the piece, so it sits within

parts.note: a seamer is a cricket bowler who makes the ball move off the seam

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A team captain puts on a bowler hat on board a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' looks like the hat, but it is a cricket bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a ship driven by steam power.

clue.text: Ready to defend a castle by the sea

parts.note: R is the chess notation for a rook, also called a castle
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A seaside fortress is prepared for attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Being equipped with weapons means being prepared to fight off attackers.

clue.text: Pity Carla drunk and incapable

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Feel sorry for Carla, who is legally drunk and incapable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk and incapable' reads as one legal phrase, but 'drunk' is the anagram signal and 'incapable' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone paralysed is unable to move; British slang also uses the word for helplessly intoxicated.

clue.text: Sedition doesn't start to make sense

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: sedition and treason are both betrayal of the state

explanation.surface: Rebellion that never begins seems sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Good sense and the power of logical thought are both called by this word.

clue.text: Refuse to relinquish barrel in service station

indicators.note: relinquishing means giving up, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: refuse here is rubbish, garbage
B is the abbreviation for barrel, as in oil prices

explanation.surface: A filling station declines to give up a barrel of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage can be a filling station selling fuel and doing car repairs.

clue.text: Show flashes of brilliance when resolving court case

indicators.note: resolving here means breaking up and settling into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A barrister dazzles while settling a legal dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To coruscate is literally to sparkle or glitter, and figuratively to be brilliantly witty.

clue.text: Mark has song for girl

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mark, as in the old German currency
an aria is a song for solo voice in opera

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark has written a song for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a female first name, and crosswords often use 'girl' to signal one.

clue.text: Girl in an anaemic state

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman is found to be suffering from anaemia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' rounds off the surface as a link: the girl is in an anaemic condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemia leaves the face pale and drained of colour, the look of grey wood remains.

clue.text: Loony enters a stream to get duck, a protected species

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it

parts.note: a rill is a small stream
loony and mad both mean crazy
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so it gives the letter O

explanation.surface: A crazy person wades into a brook to catch a duck, which is protected by law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected species' looks like conservation law, but it describes an animal in natural armour.
explanation.definitionFit: This burrowing mammal is covered in bony plates, so it is literally a shielded creature.

clue.text: Kind of shirt with a frill — that's tasty

parts.note: a T-shirt gives the letter T
a ruffle is a gathered frill on clothing

explanation.surface: A frilly shirt described as being in good taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tasty' suggests stylish clothing, but it means delicious to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the prized fungus and the chocolate sweet are delicacies prized for their flavour.

clue.text: Relative gets a warning sign that's not vindicated

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
red is the colour of danger and warning signals

explanation.surface: A family member receives a caution and remains unexonerated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose name is still under suspicion has not been exonerated or vindicated.

clue.text: Take turns to have books in class

indicators.note: to have here is to hold within, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: rate means class or grade, as in first-rate
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Pupils take it in turns to bring books to class.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate duties is to take them in turn, one after another in a cycle.

clue.text: Tory leader studied philosopher? That's soul-destroying!

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
John Stuart Mill was an English philosopher

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician read a philosopher and found it depressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull repetitive routine with no progress is described as this exercise machine, crushing to the spirit.

clue.text: Climbed like a snake

definitions.meaning: climbed up, as a mountain or ladder
covered in scales, as a reptile's skin is

explanation.surface: A snake slithered up something.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means ascended and also means covered with overlapping horny plates, as reptiles are.

clue.text: Empty bottles of French promoters

parts.note: de is French for of
admen create advertisements to promote products

explanation.surface: French advertisers have finished their drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead men is jokey slang for bottles that have been drained.

clue.text: Runs through articles

indicators.note: through puts one piece passing inside another

parts.note: pieces are items or articles
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone skims through some newspaper articles.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a run passing through articles stabs into them.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce something is to run a point right through it.

clue.text: Give satisfaction to clergyman getting contract

parts.note: P is an abbreviation for priest, a clergyman
a lease is a rental contract

explanation.surface: A vicar signs a rental agreement and is content.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to give them pleasure or contentment.

clue.text: Frank is after soldier

parts.note: since means after a time, as in 'since Tuesday'
RE is the Royal Engineers, so stands for a soldier

explanation.surface: A man named Frank follows a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and sincere both describe someone honest and genuine in what they say.

clue.text: Heartlessly ill-treated but failed to notice

indicators.note: without a heart, so the central letter is removed

parts.note: misused means abused or ill-treated

explanation.surface: Someone was cruelly abused yet nobody spotted it.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something is to overlook it entirely.

clue.text: Irene gets a bit giddy when drunk

indicators.note: giddy means reeling and dizzy, so the letters spin into a new order

explanation.surface: Irene feels slightly dizzy after drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate is a habitual drunkard, and as an adjective it means intoxicated.

clue.text: Greek captured by wanton scoundrel

indicators.note: being captured means being held inside the other piece

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute, wanton man
G is an abbreviation for Greek

explanation.surface: A Greek is taken prisoner by a lecherous villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest rascal or villain.

clue.text: Detective has a drink to start eating

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A police officer has a drink before a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase invites diners to tuck in and begin their food.

clue.text: German has file to hold firmly

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file for wood or metal

explanation.surface: A German keeps a firm grip on a metalworking tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something is to grip or seize it tightly.

clue.text: Baby appearing in Pilgrim's Progress

indicators.note: appearing in means the letters show up inside the title's words

explanation.surface: An infant character features in Bunyan's allegory The Pilgrim's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a small child or infant.

clue.text: Assistant keeps wine cold for champ

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so one piece contains the others

parts.note: a mate is a helper or assistant, as in a plumber's mate
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A helper keeps chilled wine ready for a winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champ' looks like a champion, but it is the verb meaning to chew noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to munch or chew vigorously, which is what masticating means.

clue.text: Offended indignation for failure? Gone bust!

parts.note: a dud is something that fails to work

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A failed venture has gone bankrupt, causing outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in high dudgeon is to show deep resentment at a perceived slight.

clue.text: Slip away and head off setback

indicators.note: head off means the opening letter is cut away

parts.note: a relapse is a setback, especially in recovery from illness

explanation.surface: Escaping quietly and preventing a reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes or slips by unnoticed.
